findings.issue: The `git` integration target (crates/sc-agent-types/tests/git.rs, 5 tests covering read_at_rev, the size precheck and INPUT_TOO_LARGE) is not run by `cargo test --workspace` or by a plain `cargo test -p sc-agent-types`. Nothing in the default workspace gate exercises it.
findings.recommendation: Add `cargo test -p sc-agent-types --features git --test git` (and `--features test-util --test mock`) to CI and the just/test layers. Alternatively enable `git` through a dev-dependency or feature unification so the workspace run covers it.
findings.evidence: The `Running` lines of the workspace run include tests/mock.rs but no tests/git.rs. When run explicitly the target passes with 5 tests.

findings.issue: A new `expect("Operation spellings are valid action names")` sits in a library (non-test) path. A future Operation spelling that is not a valid ActionName would panic at runtime. The unit test `every_log_operation_is_an_action_name` is the only guard.
findings.recommendation: Return a Result, or fall back to a fixed valid ActionName. Alternatively make the mapping a const or match so the invariant is checked at compile time. Keep the unit test either way.
findings.evidence: fn action_name(operation: Operation) -> ActionName { ActionName::new(operation.as_str()).expect(...) }. All other added unwrap/expect/panic hits are inside #[cfg(test)] or doc examples (sc-agent-secrets, sc-agent-types envelope/secret, sc-jev-check config/equal_input/table/questions, sc-jev-backends transport).

findings.issue: The ureq kind mapping classifies only ureq::Error::Timeout and Io(TimedOut) specially. Every other variant, including TLS/Rustls failures, DNS failures and protocol errors, maps to NetworkErrorKind::Connect. Only the pre-connect https-scheme check produces Tls (line 208), so TLS handshake failures are mislabeled as Connect.
findings.recommendation: Map ureq's TLS-specific variants (Rustls, Pki and similar) to NetworkErrorKind::Tls if retryable() or the fix_hint distinguish them. Otherwise document that Connect covers them. Add a mapping test for each branch.
findings.evidence: match error { Timeout(_) => Timeout, Io(io) => io_error_kind(io), _ => Connect }

notes: Review questions with no defect found:

EqualInputRecord Serialize (judge.rs:490): it writes the six fields in the same order, with `equal` computed from `self.equal()` and never stored. TryFrom<EqualInputWire> recomputes `equal` and rejects a mismatch with INPUT_INVALID, so the round trip is sound.

PayloadBundle::decode (payload.rs:194): it parses, re-encodes via encode (which also rejects duplicate question ids) and requires byte equality with the input. A parse failure yields encode_failed, whose code is INPUT_INVALID. The doc matches the behavior.

ErrorCode::ALL: the in-crate test at error.rs:878-912 uses a wildcard-free match (so a new variant fails to compile), checks ALL.contains, and checks uniqueness. tests/errors.rs checks ALL against errors.json. test_every_variant_code_golden compares against crate fixtures/error-codes.json, but its `every_variant()` list is hand-maintained. That is acceptable because the exhaustive in-crate match plus the errors.json comparison guard completeness.
Stderr golden fixture error-stderr.jsonl is newline-terminated JSONL (ends 0x0a) and the tests pass against it.

Session v2 reader: check_version (session/mod.rs:493) rejects a missing or older version and a newer version with session_document_invalid (INPUT_INVALID). The fixture tests/fixtures/session-v1.json is used in tests/session.rs, with the store clock set so version is the only possible failure.

read_at_rev without --no-textconv: the read path (extract/read.rs:120-190, and the same design in sc-agent-types/src/git.rs) uses `git cat-file blob <oid>`. cat-file applies no textconv or smudge filters unless --textconv or --filters is given, so output is raw filter-free blob bytes. The size precheck is intact: rev-parse --verify --end-of-options resolves once, then `cat-file -t` checks the type, `cat-file -s` is compared with MAX_INPUT_BYTES (8 MiB) before reading, and the read length is re-checked after. Tests oversize_blob_at_rev_is_input_too_large (read.rs:333) and sc-agent-types/tests/git.rs:85 cover it.

MockJudgeBackend (test_util.rs): it has no Clone and tests share it through Arc. The LLM-context refusal test exists in tests/mock.rs lines 86-104: AnthropicHaiku with a bare request returns INPUT_INVALID from both validate_for_send and judge, records nothing, and counts validations.

max_request_bytes removal: the 96 000 B limit is now BackendId::descriptor().request_limit_bytes() (catalog.rs:100-122). It is enforced pre-send on the Jev path: client/mod.rs:197 and :202 call check::prepare, which returns input_too_large (check.rs:65). The test oversized_input_is_refused_and_nothing_is_sent (sc-jev/tests/jev_api.rs:279) sends 100 000 bytes and asserts INPUT_TOO_LARGE with transport.sent() empty. packaged_config_holds_model_host_path asserts 96_000. LLM backends enforce it in sc-jev-backends validate.rs:68, with tests in tests/llm.rs lines 427 and 635. sc-jev/src/config.rs:193 tests that a `max_request_bytes` config key is now rejected.
